The petitioner is an accused in connection with  Bhubaneswar Mahila P.S. Case No.35 of 2024  corresponding to C.T. Case No.316 of 2024 for the  offences punishable under Sections 376(2)(n)/323/
506 of the IPC pending in the Court of the learned  S.D.J.M., Bhubaneswar.
The petitioner had  approached the learned Special Judge (CBI), Court  No.I-cum-Additional Sessions Judge, Bhubaneswar in  BLAPL No.780 of 2024 praying for grant of bail.

entities.text: Special Judge (CBI), Court  No.I-cum-Additional Sessions Judge, Bhubaneswar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The  learned Court below vide its order dated 30.04.2024  Page 1 of 4  rejected the bail application of the petitioner.
Being aggrieved, the petitioner has filed the present petition under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. praying for enlargement on bail.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioner, on instruction from the petitioner, submits that, except the present bail application, no other bail application of the petitioner is pending in any other Court relating to the aforesaid F.I.R.

sentences.text:
The prosecution case is that the complainant reported at Lingaraj P.S. that the present petitioner,
the P.O. of State Bank of India, Kantabanji Branch,
had kept sexual relationship with her repeatedly by giving false assurance of marriage.

entities.text: State Bank of India, Kantabanji Branch
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The petitioner also threatened her with dire consequences.

Hence, the F.I.R.
4.
During the investigation, the statement of the victim was recorded under Section 164 of the Cr. P.C.
The victim is 27 years age, whereas the petitioner is 24 years age.
The victim, in her statement has stated that both of them were in relationship.
The petitioner has exploited her keeping physical relationship with her with assurance of marriage.

5. Learned counsel for the petitioner has drawn my attention to the WhatsApp chat, which is placed on record at Annexure-3 and submits that the victim  Page 2 of 4  also demanded Rs.5 lakhs to sort out the case.
6. However, Mr. Mishra, learned counsel for the informant is seriously disputing regarding the veracity of the WhatsApp chat, which has been relied upon by learned counsel for the petitioner.
I need not go into those aspects of the matter at this stage.
7. Regard being had to the aforementioned facts and the period of custody of the petitioner since 13.03.2024 and the nature of accusation, I am inclined to admit the petitioner on bail.

8. Hence, the petitioner is directed to be released on bail by the learned Court in seisin over the matter in the aforesaid case on such terms and conditions as it would deem just and proper, subject to the following additional conditions:
(1) The petitioner shall appear before the Court, without fail, on every date of hearing; and (2) He shall not influence any of the witnesses related to this case in any manner whatsoever.

In the event the petitioner is found wanting for violation of any of the bail conditions imposed by this Court or the trial Court even on a single occasion, the prosecution is at liberty to move appropriate application before the Court below for cancellation of the concession of bail granted by this Court.
If such application is filed, the trial Court should decide the application on its own merit.
9. The BLAPL is accordingly disposed of.
